data.title: Matador Resources rises 7% amid energy sector strength
data.description:
Shares of Matador Resources (MTDR), an independent oil and natural-gas producer focused on the Delaware Basin, climbed almost 7% on Friday, rebounding after two straight sessions of losses. The advance came as the broader energy sector moved higher, even as major indices fell sharply across the board.

The stock rose $3.71 to close at $57.48.

data.title: S&P 500 ends the week lower as hot inflation and AI sell-off weigh on stocks
data.description:
Wall Street resumed its sell-off on Friday, closing 1.1% lower after a 0.3% gain on Thursday. The decline extended losses from Wednesday's roughly 1% drop in the S&P 500, as hotter-than-expected inflation data pressured market valuations.

 The S&P 500 (SP500) fell 1.9%, while the Dow (DJI) rose 0.70% and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) plunged 4.5%.

Seeking Alpha analyst Alessio Garzone highlighted, "The US inflation data was enough to bring investors back down to earth after days and weeks of euphoria. The CPI has highlighted that the inflation problem is far from resolved; indeed, high energy prices are creeping into other categories and sectors of the economy, and personally speaking, I fear that we could see new inflationary pressures in the coming months. In fact, I don't rule out the possibility of the Fed raising interest rates at upcoming meetings. Not even Warsh's words were able to do much to reassure investors.

On the microeconomic front, further cracks are beginning to emerge in the AI world, with doubts about CoreWeave and the sustainability of investments and the debt required to finance them. This is an issue that needs to be considered, distinguishing the potential of the technology from the financial sustainability of the investments behind it.

It's likely that the market is starting to ask the right questions. And that wouldn't necessarily be a bad thing."

At the sector level, seven of the 11 S&P 500 sectors ended the week in positive territory, while four closed lower. 

Consumer staples (+5.02%) and energy (+4.90%) led S&P 500 sectors higher for the week, followed by health care (+3.29%) and materials (+2.93%). 

Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman highlighted that this week saw a big sell-off in tech as the market soured on the AI trade. This brought down risk on sectors in general, alongside tech, like industrials, consumer discretionary goods, and communications. Money was not fleeing equities, just risky equities, and we see that in the top gainers of the week, all defensive sectors. Of course, energy was among the top gainer again for the week on continued squeezing in the fuel market. As long as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, I expect to continue to see energy perform well.

Conversely, technology plunged 7.65%, the worst performer, while industrials (-0.97%), consumer discretionary (-0.46%) and communication services (-0.43%) also declined.

Of the 500 stocks, 339 posted gains for the week, while 161 ended the week in negative territory.

data.title: 3 things to look out for on Monday
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages closed lower on Friday as technology stocks came under further pressure amid an already challenging trading week.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -1.1%, and the heavy-tech Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) ended -2.1%, while the blue-chip Dow (DJI) closed -0.3%.

A pullback in AI stocks weighed on the broader market this week, with memory chip stocks among the hardest-hit segments as investors reassessed the sector's recent performance.

Here are three things to look out for on Monday:

  • Some of the biggest technology names have been declining this week. Super Micro Computer (SMCI), Palo Alto Networks (PANW), Datadog (DDOG), and Seagate Technology (STX) were some top decliners in the S&P 500. Investors will continue to monitor the ongoing tech selloff.
  • On the economic calendar, investors will receive the National Association of Home Builders’ Housing Market Index. The September print showed the index had fallen lower than consensus, with builder confidence for newly built single-family homes down to its lowest level since September 2025.
  • Earnings season will continue with more companies reporting, including Fifth Third Bancorp (FITB), Steel Dynamics (STLD), W. R. Berkley (WRB), and Crown Holdings (CCK), among others.

data.title: SA analyst sees record highs ahead despite tech selloff
data.description:
Wall Street ended lower Friday as technology stocks extended their losses, although Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research maintained a bullish outlook for equities through year-end.

King said investors heavily concentrated in high-beta artificial intelligence infrastructure stocks have faced significant losses, with several names falling at least 30% from their previous week's highs.

“This week there has been much pain inflicted on anyone overly concentrated in niche high-beta AI infrastructure stocks,” King stated, highlighting the risks of concentrated exposure to volatile technology investments. 

Despite the selloff, he argued that major equity benchmarks continue to display constructive technical patterns, suggesting the recent weakness has not undermined the broader market's upward trajectory. 

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) fell -0.3% Friday. The S&P 500 (SP500) declined -1.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) plunged 2.1%.

King also noted that Treasury yields had declined considerably from the previous week, providing a potentially supportive backdrop for equities. 

“We continue to look to new ATHs into year end,” he said, maintaining his optimistic outlook despite mounting pressure on AI-related stocks.

data.title: U.S. equities tumbled lower and closed in the red as the tech selloff continued
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages finished deep in the red on Friday as technology stocks came under further pressure.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) closed -0.3%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -1.1%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) ended -2.1%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, six of the 11 segments concluded in the green, led by energy. At the other end of the spectrum, info tech struggled the most. 

A pullback in artificial intelligence-related stocks has weighed on the broader market this week, with memory chip stocks among the hardest-hit segments as investors reassessed the sector's recent performance. 

“This week there has been much pain inflicted on anyone overly concentrated in niche high-beta AI infrastructure stocks, many of which are down 30% or more from last week’s highs.  The equity indices though retain a bullish look in our view,” Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research stated.

On the economic calendar, industrial production growth accelerated more than expected in September. U.S. industrial production data  rose 0.7% M/M in September, versus the 0.4% forecasted level.

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) fell by 4 basis points to 4.71%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) ticked up 1 basis point to 5.08%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) added 1 basis point to 5.43%. 

“We think that investors should start thinking of a 5%+ 10-year Treasury yield as the new normal, not a brief aberration. For years, the Treasury enjoyed the luxury of having huge rate insensitive buyers, such as China, Japan, and the Fed, but those buyers are gone now and Treasuries have to offer competitive returns at a time when they are increasing supply due to the government’s profligate spending, which itself is giving creditors reason to require a higher rate of return,” Dennis Follmer of Montis Financial stated. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Diamondback Energy (FANG) advanced +4.2%, while shares of CoreWeave (CRWV) fell -11.9%.

data.title: Avino Silver & Gold raised to Buy at Roth on valuation, La Preciosa potential
data.description:
Avino Silver & Gold (ASM) gained 2.9% in Friday's trading as Roth Capital upgraded the precious metals miner to Buy from Neutral with a $7 price target, saying the stock's recent pullback has created a value opportunity, while the potential for positive catalysts from its La Preciosa silver project in Mexico appears on the horizon.

In addition to the value opportunity, Roth analyst Joe Reagor noted Avino (ASM) is actively examining the possibility of building a standalone mill for La Preciosa and expects the company to release a financial study in the coming months outlining the plan and then provide a timeline for potential development.

For Q3, Avino (ASM) reported silver equivalent production of 582,836 oz, up slightly from the year-earlier quarter on a consolidated basis, while development production at La Preciosa increased 5% Q/Q to 105,867 silver equivalent oz, consisting of 91,411 silver oz and 166 gold oz; Reagor said the results were "mixed" relative to his expectations.

data.title: Air Canada, United to add routes, increase flight capacity in 2027
data.description:
Air Canada (ACDVF) and United Airlines (UAL) plan to expand their Canada-US networks next summer, adding new routes and increasing flight capacity under a transborder partnership that the carriers have agreed to renew, subject to regulatory approval.

Air Canada (ACDVF) will introduce service from Toronto to Louisville on April 28, 2027, followed by flights from Montreal to Indianapolis and Edmonton to Newark beginning June 1. It will also deploy larger Airbus A220 (EADSF) aircraft on its Edmonton-San Francisco route to increase capacity.

United (UAL) plans seasonal flights between Newark and St. John's, Newfoundland, and new services linking Denver with Ottawa and Quebec City. The carrier will also increase flights between Washington, D.C., and Quebec City and boost daily seats between Denver and Winnipeg by 65%.

The expansion builds on a joint business agreement established in 2022 that has enabled 20 new transborder routes, according to Air Canada (ACDVF). The partnership supports more than 1,200 connecting itineraries between Canada and the United States.

Air Canada (ACDVF) said an application seeking approval of the renewed and expanded agreement had been submitted to Transport Canada.

The carriers said the additional services would broaden travel options and improve connections through their respective networks. The announcement comes amid softer cross-border demand in recent months.

data.title: Wells Fargo wins court order to dismiss former CEO's pay-related case - report
data.description:
A San Francisco court has ruled in favor of Wells Fargo (WFC) to dismiss former CEO Tim Sloan's $34M lawsuit, Bloomberg News reported.

In a complaint filed in 2023, Sloan claimed WFC canceled several promised stock and bonus awards between 2015 and 2019, according to the report published on Friday.

Judge Christine Van Aken granted the bank's request to resolve the case without a trial, or at least narrow the claims, on the ground that Wells Fargo made the compensation decisions using its discretion in good faith, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: FMC downgraded at Jefferies as 'visibility deteriorates, again' with guidance cut
data.description:
FMC Corp. (FMC) rebounded 1.7% in Friday's trading after plunging 31% in the previous session when the agricultural chemicals company slashed its Q3 revenue guidance to $65M-$125M, far below consensus estimates, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $510M-$565M, compared to its previous outlook for positive $120M-$140M.

Following the guidance cut, Jefferies analysts Daniel Rizzo and Charles Boakye downgraded FMC (FMC) shares to Hold from Buy with a new $5 price target, citing limited visibility, macro headwinds, and persistent pressure from generics.

The current crop protection market remains at a trough, and FMC (FMC) moved to reduce pricing on a wide range of off-patent crop protection products and simplify its North American pricing strategy, no longer using the high-gross margin, high-rebate model; as a result, the company cut its Q3 revenue and EBITDA projections, Rizzo and Boakye said.

Commodity pricing pressures will likely persist through the 2027 growing seasons, the analysts said, estimating a ~10% pricing decline next year in the core portfolio—offsetting 1%-2% volume growth—with rynaxypyr posing another $100M headwind.

On the positive side, new products including biologicals likely remain on track, and the benefits from the footprint optimization likely will be evident by H2 2027, according to Rizzo and Boakye, adding that Fluindapyr continues to ramp, and Dodhylex and Isoflex are positioned for significant growth beginning in 2028.
